newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour says minimum wage will cut welfare bill.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour says minimum wage will cut welfare bill.

text.p: Britain's Labour Party will adopt a minimum wage to stop unscrupulous employers undercutting competitors and to cut billions of pounds off the welfare bill, shadow Chancellor Gordon Brown said on Friday.
"If we don't do it, taxpayers will continue to subsidise low pay through family credit," he told BBC radio.
Family credit tops up incomes which fall below a certain level. "It's become a very expensive policy with family credit and all these benefits costing up to three billion pounds," Brown said.
"With a minimum wage, you don't have the taxpayer picking up the bills. It means you don't have good employers being undercut by bad."
Brown said the crucial question was what level the minimum wage was set at. "The proper way of setting it is through consultation....with employers and employees involved."

The ruling Conservatives reject the idea of a minimum wage, saying it will cost hundreds of thousands of jobs. In a similar vein, Prime Minister John Major is expected, on Friday, to attack Labour for backing the European Union Social Chapter, which guarantees minimum employment rights.
That too will cost jobs, the Conservatives claim.
